solution:
## Add the given percentages
\text{Total given} &= 30 + 21 + 12 + 13
&= 76
## Subtract from 100%
\text{Other} &= 100 - 76
&= 24
ANSWER: 24\%

## Find the degrees for 1%
The whole circle is 360° and represents 100%.
1\% &= \frac{360}{100}
&= 3.6^\circ
Check: $13 \times 3.6 = 46.8$, which matches the given angle.
## WC flushing
30\% &= 30 \times 3.6
&= 108^\circ
## Personal washing, baths and taps
21\% &= 21 \times 3.6
&= 75.6^\circ
## Personal washing, showers
12\% &= 12 \times 3.6
&= 43.2^\circ
## Other
24\% &= 24 \times 3.6
&= 86.4^\circ
ANSWER: 108^\circ,\ 75.6^\circ,\ 43.2^\circ,\ 46.8^\circ,\ 86.4^\circ

## Check the angles add to 360°
\text{Sum} &= 108 + 75.6 + 43.2 + 46.8 + 86.4
&= 360
## Draw the first sector
Put the protractor on the centre with its zero line along the printed radius. Measure 108° anticlockwise, draw the radius and label the sector WC flushing, 108°.
## Draw the other sectors one after another
Starting from the last radius each time, measure 75.6° (baths and taps), 43.2° (showers) and 46.8° (clothes washing). The remaining sector is Other, 86.4°, and it should end on the printed radius.
## Label every sector
Write the activity name and its angle inside each sector.
ANSWER: \text{Pie chart with sectors } 108^\circ,\ 75.6^\circ,\ 43.2^\circ,\ 46.8^\circ,\ 86.4^\circ

## Multiply for each activity
Litres used = water required per activity × frequency. One bath: $80 \times 3 = 240$ is given. Use the other rows of the table the same way (shower 125 litres, 20 showers; teeth 6 litres per minute, 32 minutes; WC flush 6 litres, 60 flushes).
\text{Shower} &= 125 \times 20
&= 2500
\text{Teeth brushing} &= 6 \times 32
&= 192
\text{WC flush} &= 6 \times 60
&= 360
\text{Washing machine} &= 45 \times 8
&= 360
\text{Dishwasher} &= 20 \times 7
&= 140
\text{Car wash} &= 10 \times 1
&= 10
\text{Hosepipe} &= 9 \times 15
&= 135
## Add all the litres
\text{Total} &= 240 + 2500 + 192 + 360 + 360 + 140 + 10 + 135
&= 3937
ANSWER: \text{Total} = 3937 \text{ litres}

## Litres used in one year
There are 52 weeks in a year.
\text{Litres} &= 3937 \times 52
&= 204\,724
## Convert to thousands of litres
\frac{204\,724}{1000} &= 204.724
## Multiply by the price per 1000 litres
\text{Cost} &= 204.724 \times \text{€}1.85
&= \text{€}378.7394
&\approx \text{€}378.74
ANSWER: \text{€}378.74

## Add 13.5% VAT
Adding 13.5% means multiplying by $1.135$.
\text{Bill} &= 378.74 \times 1.135
&= \text{€}429.8699
&\approx \text{€}429.87
ANSWER: \text{€}429.87

## Price per 1000 litres including VAT
\text{Price} &= \text{€}1.85 \times 1.135
&= \text{€}2.09975
## Find how many lots of 1000 litres €260 buys
\text{Number of lots} &= \frac{260}{2.09975}
&= 123.8242648
## Convert to litres
\text{Litres} &= 123.8242648 \times 1000
&= 123\,824.2648
&\approx 123\,824.3
ANSWER: 123\,824.3 \text{ litres}

## Read the point from the graph
Read across to the $x$-value first, then up to the $y$-value. $F$ is 4 across and 1 up.
F &= (4, 1)
ANSWER: F = (4, 1)

## Move 5 units North of F
North is straight up the page, so the $x$-value stays 4 and the $y$-value goes up by 5.
y_B &= 1 + 5
&= 6
## Plot and label the point
Plot the point $(4, 6)$ and label it $B$.
B &= (4, 6)
ANSWER: B = (4, 6)

## Use the opposite sides of the parallelogram
In $FBQT$, the side $[TQ]$ is parallel and equal to $[FB]$. $[FB]$ goes straight up 5 units, so $T$ is 5 units directly below $Q$.
x_T &= -2
y_T &= 7 - 5
&= 2
## Plot T
Plot $T(-2, 2)$ and join $F$, $B$, $Q$ and $T$ to see the parallelogram.
ANSWER: T = (-2, 2)

## Find the base [FB]
|FB| &= 6 - 1
&= 5
## Find the perpendicular height
The sides $[FB]$ and $[QT]$ are vertical, on $x = 4$ and $x = -2$. The distance between them is the height.
h &= 4 - (-2)
&= 6
## Use area = base × perpendicular height
\text{Area} &= 5 \times 6
&= 30
ANSWER: 30 \text{ square units}

## Pick out the triangle FBQ
Use triangle $FBQ$. $|\angle QFB| = 45^\circ$ is opposite $[BQ]$, and $|\angle BQF|$ is opposite $[FB]$.
$|FB| = 5$ and $|BQ| = \sqrt{37} = 6.08$.
## Write the sine rule
\frac{\sin \angle BQF}{|FB|} &= \frac{\sin 45^\circ}{|BQ|}
\frac{\sin \angle BQF}{5} &= \frac{\sin 45^\circ}{6.08}
## Multiply both sides by 5
\sin \angle BQF &= \frac{5 \sin 45^\circ}{6.08}
&= 0.5815
## Use inverse sine to find the angle
\angle BQF &= \sin^{-1}(0.5815)
&= 35.6^\circ
ANSWER: |\angle BQF| = 35.6^\circ

## Factor out the coefficient of x squared
Take out $a = 2$ so the $x^2$ term has coefficient 1.
f(x) &= 2x^2 - 7x - 10
&= 2\left(x^2 - \frac{7}{2}x - 5\right)
## Complete the square inside the bracket
Halve the coefficient of $x$: $\frac{1}{2}\times\left(-\frac{7}{2}\right) = -\frac{7}{4}$. Square it to get $\frac{49}{16}$.
x^2 - \frac{7}{2}x &= \left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{49}{16}
f(x) &= 2\left(\left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{49}{16} - 5\right)
&= 2\left(\left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{129}{16}\right)
## Multiply the 2 back in
f(x) &= 2\left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{129}{8}
ANSWER: f(x) = 2\left(x - \frac{7}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{129}{8}

## Show the graph must cross the x-axis twice
The coefficient of $x^2$ is $a = 2 > 0$, so the graph opens upwards and $f$ has a minimum point.
From part (b) the minimum is at $y = -\frac{129}{8}$, which is below the x-axis.
A graph that opens upwards with its lowest point below the x-axis must cross the x-axis twice, so $f$ has two real roots.
ANSWER: \text{Minimum is below the } x\text{-axis and } a>0 \text{, so two real roots}

## Write w in polar form
$|w| = 3$ and the angle is $30^\circ = \frac{\pi}{6}$.
w &= 3\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
## Multiply z and w
To multiply in polar form, multiply the moduli and add the angles.
zw &= 2\left(\cos\frac{5\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\times 3\left(\cos\frac{\pi}{6} + i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\right)
&= 6\left(\cos\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right) + i\sin\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{6}\right)\right)
&= 6(\cos\pi + i\sin\pi)
## Evaluate
t &= 6(-1 + 0i)
&= -6
ANSWER: t = -6

## Find f(x + h)
First principles: $f'(x) = \lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$. Replace $x$ with $x+h$ in $f$.
f(x+h) &= \frac{1}{3}(x+h)^2 - (x+h) + 3
&= \frac{1}{3}\left(x^2 + 2xh + h^2\right) - x - h + 3
&= \frac{x^2}{3} + \frac{2xh}{3} + \frac{h^2}{3} - x - h + 3
## Find f(x + h) - f(x)
f(x+h) - f(x) &= \left(\frac{x^2}{3} + \frac{2xh}{3} + \frac{h^2}{3} - x - h + 3\right) - \left(\frac{x^2}{3} - x + 3\right)
&= \frac{2xh}{3} + \frac{h^2}{3} - h
## Divide by h
\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} &= \frac{\frac{2xh}{3} + \frac{h^2}{3} - h}{h}
&= \frac{2x}{3} + \frac{h}{3} - 1
## Let h tend to 0
f'(x) &= \lim_{h\to 0}\left(\frac{2x}{3} + \frac{h}{3} - 1\right)
&= \frac{2x}{3} - 1
ANSWER: f'(x) = \frac{2x}{3} - 1

## Find the common ratio
The percentages form a geometric sequence with first term $a = 95$.
r &= \frac{42.75}{95}
&= \frac{9}{20}
## Write the inequality for the nth day
T_n &= ar^{n-1}
95\left(\frac{9}{20}\right)^{n-1} &< 0.01
\left(\frac{9}{20}\right)^{n-1} &< \frac{0.01}{95}
## Take logs of both sides
(n-1)\log\left(\frac{9}{20}\right) &< \log\left(\frac{0.01}{95}\right)
## Divide by $\log\left(\frac{9}{20}\right)$, which is negative
Dividing by a negative number reverses the inequality.
n-1 &> \frac{\log\left(\frac{0.01}{95}\right)}{\log\left(\frac{9}{20}\right)}
n-1 &> 11.47
n &> 12.47
## Choose the first whole day
$n$ must be a whole number, so the first day is the next whole number above $12.47$, which is day 13.
The marking scheme prints "12th day", but its own working gives $n > 12.47$, so the first day below 0.01% is day 13.
ANSWER: n > 12.47 \text{, so the first day is day } 13

## Substitute $x = -3$ into $f(x)$
f(-3) &= 2(-3)^3 + 5(-3)^2 - 4(-3) - 3
&= -54 + 45 + 12 - 3
&= 0
Since $f(-3) = 0$, $x = -3$ is a root and $(x+3)$ is a factor.
## Divide $f(x)$ by $(x+3)$: first term
Divide the leading terms.
2x^3 \div x &= 2x^2
Multiply back and subtract.
2x^2(x+3) &= 2x^3 + 6x^2
(2x^3 + 5x^2) - (2x^3 + 6x^2) &= -x^2
## Second term
Bring down $-4x$ and divide the leading terms.
-x^2 \div x &= -x
-x(x+3) &= -x^2 - 3x
(-x^2 - 4x) - (-x^2 - 3x) &= -x
## Third term
Bring down $-3$ and divide the leading terms.
-x \div x &= -1
-1(x+3) &= -x - 3
(-x - 3) - (-x - 3) &= 0
The remainder is $0$, so the quotient is $2x^2 - x - 1$.
## Factorise the quadratic
f(x) &= (x+3)(2x^2 - x - 1)
&= (x+3)(2x+1)(x-1)
## Read off the roots
Set each factor equal to $0$.
x + 3 &= 0
x &= -3
2x + 1 &= 0
x &= -\frac{1}{2}
x - 1 &= 0
x &= 1
ANSWER: x = -3,\ -\frac{1}{2},\ 1

## Differentiate and set $f'(x) = 0$
f'(x) &= 6x^2 + 10x - 4
6x^2 + 10x - 4 &= 0
3x^2 + 5x - 2 &= 0
## Factorise and solve
(3x - 1)(x + 2) &= 0
x &= \frac{1}{3} \text{ or } x = -2
## Decide which is the maximum
f''(x) &= 12x + 10
f''(-2) &= -14
$f''(-2) < 0$, so $x = -2$ is a local maximum.
f''\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right) &= 14
$f''\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right) > 0$, so $x = \tfrac{1}{3}$ is a local minimum.
## Find $f(-2)$
f(-2) &= 2(-2)^3 + 5(-2)^2 - 4(-2) - 3
&= -16 + 20 + 8 - 3
&= 9
## Find $f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)$
f\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right) &= 2\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^3 + 5\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2 - 4\left(\tfrac{1}{3}\right) - 3
&= \frac{2}{27} + \frac{15}{27} - \frac{36}{27} - \frac{81}{27}
&= -\frac{100}{27}
ANSWER: \text{Local max } (-2,\ 9),\quad \text{local min } \left(\tfrac{1}{3},\ -\tfrac{100}{27}\right)

## Think about the graph of $f(x) + a$
Adding $a$ moves the graph of $f$ up (or down) by $a$. A cubic has only one real root when it crosses the $x$-axis once: either the local maximum is below the axis, or the local minimum is above it.
## Local maximum below the $x$-axis
9 + a &< 0
a &< -9
## Local minimum above the $x$-axis
-\frac{100}{27} + a &> 0
a &> \frac{100}{27}
ANSWER: a < -9 \ \text{ or } \ a > \frac{100}{27}

## Rewrite $h(x)$
$h(x) = e^{-x} = \dfrac{1}{e^{x}}$, so each $h$ value is $1$ divided by the matching $g$ value.
## Make a table of values for $h(x)$
h(0) &= e^{0} = 1
h(0.2) &= e^{-0.2} \approx 0.82
h(0.4) &= e^{-0.4} \approx 0.67
h(0.6) &= e^{-0.6} \approx 0.55
h(0.8) &= e^{-0.8} \approx 0.45
h(1) &= e^{-1} \approx 0.37
## Plot and join the points
Plot $(0, 1)$, $(0.2, 0.82)$, $(0.4, 0.67)$, $(0.6, 0.55)$, $(0.8, 0.45)$ and $(1, 0.37)$, then join them with a smooth curve for $0 \le x \le 1$. It starts at the same point as $g$ and falls as $x$ increases.
ANSWER: \text{Curve through } (0,1),\ (0.2,0.82),\ (0.4,0.67),\ (0.6,0.55),\ (0.8,0.45),\ (1,0.37)

## Set up the area between the curves
From $x = 0$ the curves meet, and $g$ is above $h$ for $x > 0$, so the area runs from $x = 0$ to $x = 0.75$ with $g$ on top.
A &= \int_0^{0.75} e^{x}\,dx - \int_0^{0.75} e^{-x}\,dx
&= \int_0^{0.75} \left(e^{x} - e^{-x}\right)dx
## Integrate
$\int e^{-x}\,dx = -e^{-x}$, so $\int (e^x - e^{-x})\,dx = e^x + e^{-x}$.
A &= \left[e^{x} + e^{-x}\right]_0^{0.75}
## Substitute the limits
A &= \left(e^{0.75} + e^{-0.75}\right) - \left(e^{0} + e^{0}\right)
&= 2.1170 + 0.4724 - 2
&= 0.5894
ANSWER: 0.5894 \text{ square units}

## Substitute t = 0 into p(t)
At the beginning of 2010, $t = 0$ and the population is $1\,100\,000$.
p(0) &= S e^{0.1(0)} \times 10^6
&= S e^{0} \times 10^6
&= S \times 1 \times 10^6
&= S \times 10^6
## Set equal to 1 100 000 and solve for S
S \times 10^6 &= 1\,100\,000
S &= \frac{1\,100\,000}{10^6}
S &= 1.1
ANSWER: S = 1.1

## Substitute t = 5 into p(t)
The beginning of 2015 is $t = 5$, and $S = 1.1$.
p(5) &= 1.1 e^{0.1(5)} \times 10^6
&= 1.1 e^{0.5} \times 10^6
&= 1.813593 \times 10^6
&= 1\,813\,593
ANSWER: 1\,813\,593 \text{ people}

## Find the population at the start and end of 2015
2015 runs from $t = 5$ to $t = 6$.
p(6) &= 1.1 e^{0.6} \times 10^6
p(5) &= 1.1 e^{0.5} \times 10^6
## Subtract to find the change
p(6) - p(5) &= \left(1.1 e^{0.6} - 1.1 e^{0.5}\right) \times 10^6
&= 0.1907373 \times 10^6
&= 190\,737
ANSWER: 190\,737 \text{ people}

## Write an equation in k using t = 1
The beginning of 2011 is $t = 1$.
q(1) &= 3.9 e^{k(1)} \times 10^6
3.9 e^{k} \times 10^6 &= 3\,709\,795
## Isolate e^k
3.9 e^{k} &= 3.709795
e^{k} &= \frac{3.709795}{3.9}
## Take natural logs to solve for k
k &= \ln\left(\frac{3.709795}{3.9}\right)
k &\approx -0.0499999
k &\approx -0.05 \text{ (2 decimal places)}
ANSWER: k = -0.05

## Write the average value as an integral
The average value of $q$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 15$ is $\frac{1}{15}\int_0^{15} q(t)\,dt$.
\text{average} &= \frac{1}{15}\int_0^{15} 3.9 e^{-0.05t} \times 10^6 \, dt
## Integrate and substitute the limits
$\int e^{kt}\,dt = \frac{e^{kt}}{k}$.
\text{average} &= \frac{10^6}{15} \times \frac{3.9}{-0.05}\left[e^{-0.05t}\right]_0^{15}
&= \frac{10^6}{15} \times (-78)\left(e^{-0.75} - e^{0}\right)
&= \frac{10^6}{15} \times (-78)(0.4723666 - 1)
&= \frac{10^6}{15} \times (-78)(-0.5276334)
&= 2.743694 \times 10^6
&= 2\,743\,694
ANSWER: 2\,743\,694 \text{ people}

## Differentiate q(t)
q(t) &= 3.9 e^{-0.05t} \times 10^6
The derivative of $e^{kt}$ is $k e^{kt}$.
q'(t) &= -0.05 \times 3.9 e^{-0.05t} \times 10^6
## Substitute t = 8
The beginning of 2018 is $t = 8$.
q'(8) &= -0.05 \times 3.9 e^{-0.05(8)} \times 10^6
&= -0.195 e^{-0.4} \times 10^6
&= -0.195 \times 0.670320 \times 10^6
&= -130\,712
ANSWER: -130\,712 \text{ people per year}

## Find 2.5% of the original debt
A &= \frac{2.5}{100} \times 5000
&= 125
ANSWER: \text{€}125

## Set up the equivalent monthly rate
An APR of 21.75% multiplies a balance by $1.2175$ over 12 months. If the monthly rate is $i$, then $(1+i)^{12} = 1.2175$.
(1+i)^{12} &= 1.2175
## Take the 12th root
1+i &= 1.2175^{\frac{1}{12}}
1+i &\approx 1.016535
i &\approx 0.016535
As a percentage, $i \approx 1.65\%$ to 3 significant figures.
ANSWER: 1.65\%

## Month 1: interest is 1.65% of the balance, and the payment is €125
Each month the interest is $1.65\%$ of the previous balance. The part of the €125 payment left after the interest reduces the debt.
\text{Interest} &= 0.0165 \times 5000
&= 82.50
\text{Previous balance reduced by} &= 125 - 82.50
&= 42.50
\text{New balance} &= 5000 - 42.50
&= 4957.50
## Month 2
\text{Interest} &= 0.0165 \times 4957.50
&\approx 81.80
\text{Previous balance reduced by} &= 125 - 81.80
&= 43.20
\text{New balance} &= 4957.50 - 43.20
&= 4914.30
## Month 3
\text{Interest} &= 0.0165 \times 4914.30
&\approx 81.09
\text{Previous balance reduced by} &= 125 - 81.09
&= 43.91
\text{New balance} &= 4914.30 - 43.91
&= 4870.39
ANSWER: \text{Payment } 1\text{: } 125,\ 82.50,\ 42.50,\ 4957.50 \quad \text{Payment } 2\text{: } 125,\ 81.80,\ 43.20,\ 4914.30 \quad \text{Payment } 3\text{: } 125,\ 81.09,\ 43.91,\ 4870.39

## Find the weekly interest rate
An APR of 8.5% multiplies a balance by $1.085$ over 52 weeks, so $(1+i)^{52} = 1.085$.
(1+i)^{52} &= 1.085
1+i &= 1.085^{\frac{1}{52}}
1+i &\approx 1.00157
i &\approx 0.00157
## Substitute P = 5000, i = 0.00157 and t = 156 into the formula
A &= \frac{P\, i (1+i)^t}{(1+i)^t - 1}
&= \frac{5000(0.00157)(1.00157)^{156}}{(1.00157)^{156} - 1}
&\approx 36.16
ANSWER: \text{€}36.16

## Total paid to the credit card company
\text{Total} &= 125 \times 66
&= \text{€}8250
## Total paid to the Credit Union
\text{Total} &= 36.16 \times 156
&= \text{€}5640.96
## Subtract to find the saving
\text{Saving} &= 8250 - 5640.96
&= \text{€}2609.04
ANSWER: \text{€}2609.04
